fixture_name: Milltown Park toucan-crossing VRU conflicts — real Irish Stage 1 RSA incl. rejected recommendation (ABP 322160)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Constrained shared-use space at a toucan crossing due to footpath width plus signal pole/lighting column obstructions is a genuine, scheme-relevant collision risk appropriate to raise at preliminary design.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-IN-025 supplies a verbatim quote of the recorded problem statement that directly supports the pivotal constrained-space and collision-potential claim.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed solely as a safety concern with no compliance assertion, consistent with PIARC-derived international baseline semantics at preliminary design stage.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable—relocate the lighting column and provide a single set of pedestrian/vehicular signal heads—directly addressing the obstruction identified and viable at design stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly named as affected user groups and the cyclist-pedestrian interaction within shared space is the core of the concern.

justifications.substance: Shared-use width insufficiency creating pedestrian/cyclist conflict risk is a genuine, substantive vulnerable-user safety concern appropriate to preliminary design stage.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is anchored by verbatim quoted evidence EV-IN-026 stating the width 'may not be sufficient to cater for both user groups and could lead to collisions'; no invented content.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed purely as a safety concern with no compliance conflation, and rejection history is correctly quarantined in reviewer_note/provenance rather than treated as audit substance.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation is specific (named approach and access), actionable (widen shared-use area), and viable as a preliminary-design-stage design change request.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are the explicit subject of the concern, with their interaction risk directly assessed.
